ext_desc.message: Lets Daimond operate a real site in a real tab, in your browser, with your session. No credential ever leaves the device.

popup_take.message: Hand the wheel back to Daimond

popup_mirror.message: Allow the live view of the tab

popup_none.message: None yet. Daimond must ask before it touches any site.

popup_any_tab.message: Any tab, for the live view

popup_machine_hand_origin.message: Running commands on this computer, for $ORIGIN$

popup_ask_mirror.message: Waiting for you: may Daimond show the tab it is driving?

popup_ask_mirror_fine.message: It needs to photograph the tab, which Chrome cannot allow site by site. Saying no costs nothing — Daimond works from the page structure instead.

popup_ask_site.message: Waiting for you: may Daimond operate $HOST$?

popup_ask_site_fine.message: Approving covers $HOST$ and its subdomains, and nothing else. Chrome asks once more to confirm.

popup_ask_hand.message: Waiting for you: may Daimond run commands on this computer?

popup_ask_hand_fine.message: It would run builds, tests and scripts as you. Saying no costs nothing — Daimond keeps working in the browser instead.

popup_mode_user_fine.message: Daimond is not watching this tab: no page, no pixels, no keystrokes.

popup_mode_agent_fine.message: Passwords and payment fields are never sent, even now.

grant_more.message: What this covers, and what it does not

grant_mirror_head.message: Daimond wants to show you the tab it is driving

grant_mirror_body.message: To show the tab inside the Daimond panel, the extension needs to take a picture of it. Chrome will not allow that site by site, so this permission covers any tab.

grant_mirror_fine.message: It changes nothing about the handoff: while you are entering a password, no picture is taken and none is sent. You can withdraw this at any time from the Daimond Hands icon. If you say no, Daimond simply works from the page structure instead.

grant_site_head.message: Daimond wants to operate a site for you

grant_site_scope.message: This covers $HOST$ and its subdomains, and nothing else. Every other site is asked separately.

grant_site_body.message: Daimond can read this site’s page structure and click and type on it, in this browser, as you.

grant_site_fine.message: When you click below, Chrome asks once more — it will say “read and change your data on this site”, which is Chrome’s standard wording for any extension, not something extra Daimond does. That prompt is the real approval, and it only appears the first time for a site. Daimond never sees a password: the moment a login form appears it stops receiving anything until you hand the wheel back, and you can withdraw this at any time from the Daimond Hands icon.

grant_hand_head.message: Daimond wants to run commands on this computer

grant_hand_lead.message: Programs would run on this computer as you, with your files. This machine can hold them to one folder — inside it, they can read and change anything.

grant_hand_lead_nofence.message: Programs would run on this computer as you, with your files. This machine cannot limit which files they touch, so a command reaches everything you can reach.

grant_hand_lead_unknown.message: Programs would run on this computer as you, with your files. This machine did not say what it can limit them to, so treat a command as reaching everything you can reach.

grant_hand_strongest.message: This is the strongest thing you can allow Daimond to do.

grant_hand_body.message: Daimond would run programs on this computer — builds, tests, scripts — as you, with your files. Each one is started directly rather than through a shell, and only inside the folders the workspace already allows.

grant_hand_body_nofence.message: Daimond would run programs on this computer — builds, tests, scripts — as you, with your files. Each one is started directly rather than through a shell. This computer cannot limit which files they touch, so a command you allow here reaches everything you can reach.

grant_hand_body_unknown.message: Daimond would run programs on this computer — builds, tests, scripts — as you, with your files. Each one is started directly rather than through a shell. The hand here did not say what it can limit them to, so treat a command as reaching everything you can reach.

grant_hand_fine.message: Nothing runs until you allow it here, every run is written to a journal you can read, and you can withdraw this at any time from the Daimond Hands icon. Withdrawing it stops whatever is running at that moment.

grant_hand_caps_unknown.message: The hand on this computer did not say what it can enforce.

grant_hand_fine_nojournal.message: Nothing runs until you allow it here, only the page named above may ask, and you can withdraw this at any time from the Daimond Hands icon. Withdrawing it stops whatever is running at that moment.

action_pending_mirror.message: Daimond Hands — waiting for you to allow the live view

action_pending_site.message: Daimond Hands — waiting for you to approve $HOST$

action_pending_hand.message: Daimond Hands — waiting for you to allow commands on this computer

raise_none.message: Nothing is waiting to be approved.

raise_gone.message: That window has gone. Ask Daimond to open the site again.
